page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1d, 2 MB of L2, and 260 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration engines. Local storage consists of a bundled 1888 GB NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent median-tier to upper-tier computational throughput. The instance scored 1924.0 in Geekbench single-core and 15710.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside an overall PassMark CPU score of 47243.56. While PassMark memory testing was in the bottom quartile, uncached large-block read bandwidth achieved 138.52 GB/sec. The instance shows notable strength in specialized processing: Geekbench image and text processing tests placed in the top 25%, as did static web serving throughput at 56.21 GB/sec and small-model LLM prompt processing. Text generation on lightweight LLMs (135M) reached the top 10% tier at 355.44 tokens per second.

The D32ds_v6 delivers favorable resource density for multi-tenant and I/O-intensive workloads requiring dedicated compute without the premium attached to memory-skewed or GPU-accelerated tiers. The primary architectural tradeoff is standard memory subsystem latency against high vector computation capability and fast local NVMe storage. Suitable workloads include static web serving, enterprise databases requiring high local disk capacity, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and CPU-based lightweight AI inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 128.0 GB of system memory, and a integrated 1888 GB local NVMe SSD. It features modern CPU instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, but does not include GPU hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect solid mid-to-high tier performance, characterized by strong static web throughput at 56.21 GB/sec, rapid small-model language model inference, and solid image processing scores, despite modest raw memory benchmark results. With balanced compute-to-memory ratios and substantial low-latency local disk space, the D32ds_v6 is well suited for high-traffic web servers, compilation workloads, relational databases, and batch data processing.
